title: Research: prove higher-target star-code hierarchies and decoder geometry
body:
Research contribution with uniform proofs and exact finite certificates; **no new κ or physical supplier**.

This determines how much simultaneous information global proper-star observations can expose after puncturing. It extends the original asymmetric decoder obstruction into sharp one-/two-target geometry, a complete graph-case hierarchy, and uniform higher-target theorems. The new exception is concrete: at `q=p-k=2,k>=4`, a localized affine cube decodes three selectable targets using eleven deletions, beating every three-minimum-star span. Four and five selectable targets also need exactly eleven deletions.

### Completed results

- **Every available rank at k=2:** complete generalized-weight hierarchies with and without the empty star, including their higher-rank differences and the p=2 exception. Graph witnesses lift to rigorous upper bounds for higher k.
- **Every k>=2,q>=3:** the first two nonzero word weights are `2q+2` and `4q+2`. There are no intermediate weights. The third generalized weight is `6q+3`; every optimum is a triangle of minimum stars, with exactly `2^(k+1) binom(p,k-2) binom(q+2,3)` such subcodes.
- **Prescribed triples, q>=3:** exactly `6q` deletions suffice iff the three target columns are independent on some optimal triangle. Larger budgets for triples failing that criterion are not classified.
- **The complete q=2 third-weight boundary:** `d3=15` for k=2,3; for every k>=4, the first five generalized weights are `(6,11,14,15,16)`.
- **Earlier results retained:** uniform minimum-word rigidity, complete optimal two-dimensional-subcode classification, and the exact prescribed-pair budget (`4q+1` when signed intersection is at least k−2; otherwise `4q+2`), plus the original unpunctured and target-local results.

A generalized weight `d_r` gives the exact `d_r-r` deletion budget for **some selectable r-target set**. It does not assign that budget to every prescribed set. Code statements cover both proper-star spaces; the original uniform overlap corrections are absorbed only at power-of-two k. Exact nonlinear postprocessing of these same observations does not improve the information thresholds.

### Review and reproduction

Only `research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/` changes. Start with its README, then `HIGHER-GRAPH.md` and `HIGHER-WEIGHTS.md`. The latest extension is separated into graph/checker commit `76f007ab` and uniform-theorem/cube commit `7d526020`.

```sh
for check in higher cube boundary; do
  python3 -I -O -B "research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/${check}_verify.py" --self-test || exit
done
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/global_verify.py --self-test
python3 -I -O -B research/asymmetric-hypercube-decoder/verify.py --negative-controls
```

Expected prefixes: `PASS_HIGHER_GRAPH`, `PASS_CUBE`, `PASS_K3_BOUNDARY`, `PASS_GLOBAL_EQUALITY`, and `PASS`.

The new checks include four complete graph partition DPs, 8,224 literal edge restrictions, 449,606 complete small-code subspaces, **7,135,750 rank-three subspaces**, and weight distributions of 523,776 graph-code words. They verify 68 optimal graph decoders with 1,511 full-code restoration controls; fifteen cube decoders on full port families with 165 displayed-subcode restoration controls; and all five shortening spaces in the exceptional k=3 boundary. The cube receipts contain literal proper-star expansions, targets, deletions, coefficients, and scalar cost counts.

Python 3.11.13 and 3.14.5 produce byte-identical new receipts under isolated optimized execution. Relocation, receipt corruption rejection, output preservation, inherited checker replays, and immutable source hashes pass. Proofs and code received separate AI-assisted reviews; no independent human or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Finite enumeration supports the written uniform proofs rather than replacing them. Unrelated repository-wide regeneration, selected supplier cold replay, and hosted CI are not claimed.

### Provenance and limits

Original base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; higher-target continuation base: `8bcbaafe8590d30eff9c0ae5fd9e49479c84038c`. Final main context remains `f567884aeb8851b6e794af1184119a3bfbe1e631`, selecting conditional κ `1661634653669567/10^18` from #799 with #741/#589. The selected certificate and `upstream/` are unchanged. Seed **48**, structural decoder research. Local claims record scope, pins, coverage, and unresolved questions; overlap metadata was refreshed through #876, including the distinct E8 geometry of #875.

Credit **Luke Mansoor (#732)** for uniform minimum distance, **Sagar Thakrar (#725)** for the q=1 exception, **Alishan Ladhani (#747)** for the finite (6,4) minimum-word classification, **ellipsi2 (#772)** for uniform ranks, and **Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled (#231)** with **icekylinx/eumemic** for the earlier paired-cube decoder lineage. Exact heads and text hashes remain in `EXTENSION-CLAIM.json` and `HIGHER-CLAIM.json`. The known binary incidence-code/cut bridge is credited to Martínez-Bernal, Valencia-Bucio, and Villarreal, [arXiv:1812.04106v2, Corollary 2.13](https://arxiv.org/html/1812.04106v2); no literature-wide priority claim is made for the graph invariant.

`HIGHER-COST.md` prices the displayed naive scalar schedule and identifies the unresolved source-access, helper, frame, copy/restoration, recursive-child, and assembly obligations. A deletion count is not a paid supplier invoice. Full higher-k hierarchies beyond the stated ranks and exact larger prescribed-triple budgets remain open.

Prepared by **Sam Sung (@the-missionary-company)** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including proof development, implementation, and independent AI-assisted review. Apache-2.0.
